response.original_title: A Better Way: James Lawson, Architect of Nonviolence
response.overview: he Rev. James Lawson was an unsung founder of the Civil Rights Movement who helped shape it through faith, moral clarity, and nonviolence. A close colleague of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., he later confronted racism, police violence, and apartheid. Featuring rare archival footage and reflections from civil rights leaders past and present, this compelling portrait offers a fresh perspective on American history and a timely reminder of the importance of speaking truth to power
